text:
Alex: Quick sync — we need a final acceptance checklist for Dedicated + Private v2 by Tue EOD. Focus areas: SLA commitments, pricing floor, docs coverage, support playbooks, monitoring alerts. Flag blockers now.

Sam: On SLA targets — propose `p99 < 120ms` for inference latency on Dedicated reserved pools and `99.95%` monthly uptime. Private deployments SHOULD be documented as 'customer-managed availability' with a supported SLA option. Thoughts? :eyes:

Henry: Infra note: we can target `p99 < 120ms` under normal load for reserved pools, but must call out maintenance windows and burst throttling behavior. Need to add capacity headroom number (e.g., +25% buffer) into the SLA appendix. I'll link capacity calcs.

Claire: From SE/customer ask: include an explicit fallback policy if Dedicated capacity is exhausted. Recommend automatic routing to hosted equivalent with customer opt-in during onboarding, and clear billing implications. Need legal sign-off.

Jen: Legal: fallback opt-in approach is OK if we capture explicit consent and billing detail up-front. Also require a short data residency clause for Private customers (what we can/can't access, support flows). I'll draft language.

Mario: Support: we need concrete playbooks for two incident classes: (1) degradation impacting p99 across a pool, (2) tenant isolation/auth incidents. Also need an SLA-credit calculator for billing to use. Can we get runbook drafts by EOD Fri?

Nina: QA: I'll own acceptance tests for SLA verification. Plan: synthetic workload harness that measures 50/95/99 percentiles across sequence lengths and concurrency profiles. Need testbed IDs and capacity stamps from infra to run reproducible tests.

Liz: Docs: I'll prepare two pages — 'Customer acceptance checklist' (what customers must validate) and 'Operator runbook & escalation matrix' (for Redwood on-call). Need finalized SLA numbers, fallback policy copy, and support tiers. ETA EOD Fri if I get inputs today.

Claire: Monitoring suggestions: create alerts when p99 > 80ms sustained for 5m, or error rate > 0.5% for 1m. Map alerts to SE severity and support playbooks. Also add a synthetic health check every 30s with anomaly detection.

Alex: Owners (please ack + ETA): Henry = infra capacity + testbed IDs, Nina = QA harness & acceptance tests, Liz = docs, Mario = support playbooks, Jen = legal consent/billing language, Sam = finalize SLA wording, Claire = fallback policy + alert thresholds.

Henry: ack — I can deliver capacity numbers and testbed IDs by Thu 12:00 UTC.

Nina: ack — QA harness ready for first run Thu 18:00 UTC once Henry's IDs are in.

Liz: ack — will draft docs and aim to have first pass Fri EOD.

Mario: ack — support playbooks draft by Fri EOD, will include escalation matrix and credit calc stub.

Jen: ack — legal copy by Fri EOD; will include consent snippet and residency clause.

Sam: ack — I'll firm up SLA text and exception language today.

Claire: ack — fallback policy + alert thresholds done Thu 16:00 UTC.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout queued for the Dedicated v2 stack once acceptance doc is merged. See CI pipeline: `infra/ci/pipelines/dedicated-v2/canary`.

Alex: Great — thanks everyone. I'll collate these into a single acceptance statement and circulate to sales and legal tomorrow morning. If any blocker emerges, @here escalate immediately. :thumbsup:
